newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Re looks to stay on expansion path.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Re looks to stay on expansion path.

text.p: Swiss Reinsurance Co's discussions on a possible purchase of Unione Italiana di Riassicurazione SpA could be positive for the world's second largest reinsurer, but analysts were waiting for more details.
Swiss Re said late on Monday it was in talks with Italy's Istituto Nazionale delle Assicurazioni (INA) to buy Unione Italiana di Riassicurazione SpA, considered Italy's largest reinsurer.

"Swiss Re has only two percent of gross premiums coming from Italy. This could boost gross premiums in Italy to as much as $1 billion making it one of the more important businesses for the group," said Thomas Della Putta, insurance analyst at Pictet & Cie in Geneva.

Swiss Re said in a statement late on Monday that it was in talks with Istituto Nazionale delle Assicurazioni SpA which, "subject to corporate approvals and regulatory clearances, might lead to the acquisition of Unione Italiana di Riassicurazione SpA by Swiss Re from INA."

Swiss Re, described by some analysts as company which takes an "opportunistic" approach to acquisition, in August bought out Mercantile and General Re, Britain's oldest and largest reinsurance firm after passing on American Re, which was acquired by Germany's Munich Re.
Swiss Re bought M&G Re from Britain's Prudential Corp for around 3.15 billion Swiss francs in cash.
Reinsurers have generally been seen eager to join forces amid downward pressure on profit margins.
This most recent Swiss Re move follows a consolidation wave in the industry which has reduced the number of major players.
"It (an acquisition) would be a good geographic expansion in southern Europe," Bank Julius Baer analyst Beat Alpiger.
Both analysts said they did not expect the Swiss company to go through with an acquisition if it would prove to be dilutive.
"Without any financial details it is difficult to make a judgement, but it will probably go on the same lines as M&G and will not be dilutive for shareholders or for the group," Della Putta said.

CS Investment Research analyst Heinrich-Horst Wiemer notes that it would be highly unlikely for Swiss Re to pay more than the equivalent of 1.3 times premiums that it paid for M&G, a more profitable and diverse company.

He also said Swiss Re is in a strong bargaining position in view of the fact that INA has said it wants to sell Unione and, with the improved geographic spread and operating leverage obtained from the M&G acquisition, there is hardly any pressure on the Swiss company to make any deal at all.
"Right now they are in a comfortable position," he said.
He also said he is now looking forward to an analysts' meeting with Swiss Re scheduled for December 6 in which more should be revealed.
Swiss Re's ordinary after-tax profit jumped 54 percent in 1995 to 1.09 billion francs. It has said it expects 1996 profit to rise significantly as well.

Preliminary data from Unione Italiana di Riassicurazione showed 1995 profits rising 45 percent to 25.2 billion lire with gross premiums up 7.1 percent to 1,504 billion. -- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340
